title: Drill 5 · Friday Ready 🚀
subject: Maths
focus: Who does the question ask about?
source_note: Revision for the class test on Fri 2026-10-09. Spaced revisit of every Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 error (P1 Q13, Q14, Q27, Q28; P2 Q5, Q9, Q10, Q12, Q17) with new numbers, plus Maths_Brain Priority Topics and older logged slips (topictest4, 2026-07-10, 2026-07-17, 2026-05-15, 2026-03, 2026-02-14). π = 3.14.

questions.stem: Four dogs have an average mass of 25 kg. Each dog has a DIFFERENT whole-number mass, and each is at least 20 kg. What is the greatest possible mass of the heaviest dog?
questions.explanation: Total = 4 × 25 = 100 kg. Make the other three as light as possible AND different: 20 + 21 + 22 = 63 kg. Heaviest = 100 − 63 = 37 kg.
questions.technique: Underline condition words first: 'different', 'at least', 'whole number'.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P1 Q13 (missed 'different masses'); revisit of Drill 4 f1

questions.stem: A school has 150 pupils and 40% of them are girls. Then 30 more girls join the school. What percentage of the pupils are girls now?
questions.explanation: Girls at first: 40% of 150 = 60. After: 60 + 30 = 90 girls. The school grew too: 150 + 30 = 180 pupils. 90 out of 180 = 50%.
questions.technique: People join or leave → the part AND the total change. New part ÷ NEW total.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P1 Q14 (66/120 instead of 66/132)

questions.stem: Ken spent 30% of his savings on a phone. Then he spent 3/7 of the REMAINING money on a jacket. He had $480 left.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How much were his savings at first?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How much did the jacket cost?

solution: The jacket takes 3/7 of that 70%, so 4/7 of the 70% is left: 4/7 × 70% = 40%.
(b) Money after the phone = 70% of 1200 = $840. Jacket = 3/7 × 840 = $360.
questions.technique: Bar model: cut off 30%, then split ONLY the leftover part into sevenths.
questions.trap: Taking 3/7 of ALL his savings (30% + 43% gone)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P2 Q10 (Robin, 3/5 of the remaining); spaced revisit of Drill 4 w1/w2

asks_for.prompt: Before you start: the 3/7 is a fraction of…
options: The money left after the phone

questions.stem: Simplify (3x²)³
questions.explanation: The power goes on EVERYTHING inside the bracket: 3³ × (x²)³ = 27 × x⁶ = 27x⁶.
questions.technique: Power of a power: MULTIPLY the indices. The number gets the power too: 3³ = 27, not 3 × 3.
questions.source: Maths_Brain Priority #1 (Indices); Test_Analysis_2026-03-19, 2026-03-09

questions.stem: Rectangles A and B overlap. Area of A : area of B = 4 : 3. The SHADED part is the part of B that is NOT inside A, and it is 2/3 of the area of B. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area of the whole figure?
questions.explanation: Let A = 12 units, B = 9 units. Shaded = 2/3 × 9 = 6 units, overlap = 9 − 6 = 3 units. The unshaded part is all of A (overlap included) = 12 units. Shaded : unshaded = 6 : 12 = 1 : 2.
questions.technique: Split the figure into 3 regions FIRST: A only, overlap, B only. The overlap is counted once.
questions.trap: Using A + B = 21 as the whole (6 : 15 = 2 : 5), counting the overlap twice
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P2 Q5 (answered 1:10, correct 5:12)

questions.explanation: Powers first: (−2)² = 4. Then ÷ and ×: −12 ÷ −3 = 4 and 4 × 4 = 16. Then add: 4 + 16 = 20.
questions.technique: BIDMAS, and (−2)² = (−2) × (−2) = +4. Negative ÷ negative = positive.
questions.source: Mistake_Tracker Test 1 (2026-06-18) negative numbers / order of operations

questions.stem: A quarter circle of radius 12 cm is cut out of a 12 cm square, centred at one corner. The shaded part is what is left. (Use π = 3.14)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the perimeter of the shaded part.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the area of the shaded part.

solution: (a) Trace the shaded edge: two straight sides of the square (12 + 12 = 24 cm) and the curved arc.
Quarter arc = 2 × 3.14 × 12 ÷ 4 = 18.84 cm (that's πr ÷ 2, not πr ÷ 4).
questions.technique: Perimeter: trace the edge of the SHADED part with your finger. Quarter arc = 2πr ÷ 4.
questions.trap: Using πr/4 = 9.42 for the arc; adding all 4 square sides
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P2 Q12a (πr/4 slip), Q12b (area blank), P1 Q27 (perimeter of shaded parts)

asks_for.prompt: The perimeter of the shaded part is made of…
options: 2 sides of the square + the curved arc

questions.stem: Factorise FULLY: 6x²y + 9xy
questions.explanation: HCF of the numbers: 3. HCF of the letters: x and y are in both terms. HCF = 3xy. 6x²y ÷ 3xy = 2x and 9xy ÷ 3xy = 3. So 6x²y + 9xy = 3xy(2x + 3).
questions.technique: Fully = take out the number AND every letter they share. Check: nothing left inside has a common factor.
questions.trap: Taking out only the number 3 (or only x, or only xy)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-topictest4-datetbd Q3c (only factored out the numeral)

questions.stem: Three identical squares share the corner P. The bottom side of the left square lies on a straight line. Use the marked angles to find x.
questions.explanation: Name the small slices at P from left to right: 30°, a, x, b, 25°. Each square's corner is 90°: left square 30 + a + x = 90, middle square a + x + b = 90, right square x + b + 25 = 90. The first two give b = 30. Then x + 30 + 25 = 90, so x = 35°. (Short cut: x = 90 − 30 − 25.)
questions.technique: Label every slice at the shared corner (a, b, x) and write one '= 90' equation per square.
questions.trap: Copying one of the marked angles (25° or 30°)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P1 Q28 (three squares, abandoned; answer 27°); revisit of Drill 4 f12

questions.stem: A toaster costs $143 including 10% GST. What is its price BEFORE GST?
questions.explanation: Price with GST = 110% of the price before GST. 110% = $143, so 10% = $13 and 100% = $130.
questions.technique: Reverse percentage: the $143 is 110%, not 100%. Divide by 110, times 100.
questions.source: Maths_Brain Priority #3 (reverse %); Test_Analysis_2026-07-17 P2 Q1 (GST)

questions.stem: Simplify: (x + 3)/4 − (x − 1)/6
questions.explanation: Common denominator 12: 3(x + 3)/12 − 2(x − 1)/12 = (3x + 9 − 2x + 2)/12 = (x + 11)/12. The minus goes on BOTH terms of 2(x − 1): −2x and +2.
questions.technique: Put the second numerator in brackets before subtracting: − (2x − 2) = −2x + 2.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-topictest4-datetbd Q8d (sign error subtracting fractions)

questions.stem: Find the area of the shaded ring. (Use π = 3.14)
questions.technique: Ring = big circle − small circle. Square each radius separately; don't subtract the radii first.
questions.source: Circles_Composite_Shapes common mistakes; Test_Analysis_2025-10-01 Q17/Q20 (annulus)

questions.stem: Ben has some cards. Cal has twice as many as Ben. Dan has 8 more than Cal. Altogether they have 68 cards. How many cards does CAL have?
questions.explanation: Let Ben = x. Cal = 2x, Dan = 2x + 8. x + 2x + 2x + 8 = 68, so 5x = 60 and x = 12. But the question asks for CAL: 2 × 12 = 24.
questions.technique: Circle WHO the question asks about before you start, and check it again before you write the answer.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-07-17 P2 Q6 (answered for the wrong person)

questions.stem: A $80 game goes UP in price by 20%. Later the new price goes DOWN by 25%. What is the overall change compared with the original $80?
questions.technique: Each new percentage is of the NEW price. Work it out in dollars, then compare with the ORIGINAL.
questions.source: Percentages common mistakes (multi-step chains); Maths_Brain Priority #3

questions.stem: Mia, Noah and Zara each had n stickers. Mia gave 1/3 of her stickers to Noah. Then Noah gave 1/4 of ALL his stickers to Zara. In the end, Zara had 12 more stickers than Mia.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many stickers did Zara have in the end?

solution: Make a table. Start: Mia n, Noah n, Zara n.
Mia gives n/3: Mia = 2n/3, Noah = 4n/3, Zara = n.
Noah gives 1/4 of 4n/3 = n/3: Noah = n, Zara = 4n/3.
questions.technique: One row per step, one column per person. Keep everything in n until the end.
questions.trap: Taking 1/4 of Noah's ORIGINAL n instead of all his stickers after Mia's gift
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P2 Q17 (5-mark transfer problem, not reached); revisit of Drill 4 w6

questions.stem: A puppy's mass went from 6.4 kg to 8 kg. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 8 − 6.4 = 1.6 kg. Percentage increase = 1.6 ÷ 6.4 × 100% = 25%.
questions.technique: Percentage change = change ÷ ORIGINAL × 100%. Copy the given numbers carefully.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-07-10 P1 Q25 (misread the given number); Mistake_Tracker 2026-07-10

questions.stem: At a camp, the ratio of boys to girls is 5 : 3. After 12 boys go home, there are the same number of boys and girls. How many GIRLS are at the camp?
questions.explanation: Girls don't change. Boys 5 units, girls 3 units. Boys − 12 = girls, so 2 units = 12 and 1 unit = 6. Girls = 3 × 6 = 18.
questions.technique: Find what stays the same (the girls). The change (12) matches the difference in units (5 − 3 = 2).
questions.trap: Giving the boys (30) or one unit (6)
questions.source: Ratio_Proportion common mistakes (ratio changes partway); Maths_Brain Priority #5

questions.stem: Write 0.00045 in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 4 places right to get 4.5 (a number from 1 to 10). The number is small, so the power is negative: 4.5 × 10⁻⁴.
questions.technique: Small number (less than 1) → negative power. The front number must be between 1 and 10.
questions.trap: Positive power (10⁴), or 45 × 10⁻⁵ (front number not between 1 and 10)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-03-09 / 2026-03-19 (scientific notation sign errors)

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 48°. BC is extended to D. Find ∠ACD.
questions.explanation: AB = AC, so the base angles are equal: (180 − 48) ÷ 2 = 66°. ∠ACB = 66°. ∠ACD is on a straight line with ∠ACB: 180 − 66 = 114°.
questions.technique: Spot the equal sides (tick marks) → equal base angles. Then use the straight line.
questions.source: Maths_Brain Priority #4 (angle geometry in composite figures)

questions.stem: Zoe puts $500 in the bank at 4% per year SIMPLE interest. How much money will she have in the bank after 3 years (savings + interest)?
questions.explanation: Interest each year = 4% of $500 = $20. For 3 years: 3 × $20 = $60. Total = $500 + $60 = $560.
questions.technique: Simple interest: the same amount every year (I = P × r × T). Read whether they want the interest or the TOTAL.
questions.trap: Answering only the interest ($60) or using compound interest ($562.43)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-02-14 Q20-22 (simple vs compound); Maths_Brain Priority #7

questions.stem: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 5. If C = 50, what is A?
questions.explanation: Make B the same in both: A : B = 9 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 10. So A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 10. C = 10 units = 50, so 1 unit = 5 and A = 9 × 5 = 45.
questions.technique: To join two ratios, make the shared letter (B) the same number using the LCM.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-07-10 P1 Q11 (didn't combine the second ratio); Ratio common mistakes

questions.stem: In a class, 2/5 of the pupils are girls. 3/4 of the girls and 1/3 of the boys wear glasses. What fraction of the WHOLE class wears glasses?
questions.explanation: Girls with glasses = 3/4 of 2/5 = 3/10. Boys are 3/5 of the class, so boys with glasses = 1/3 of 3/5 = 1/5. Total = 3/10 + 2/10 = 5/10 = 1/2.
questions.technique: 'of' means × . Each fraction is of a DIFFERENT group, so change each to a fraction of the whole class first.
questions.trap: Adding 3/4 and 1/3 or averaging them (13/24); forgetting the boys (3/10)
questions.source: Fractions common mistakes (fraction-of-remainder / combinations, class notes 2024-06-30)

questions.stem: A cyclist rides 18 km in 45 minutes. What is her average speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: 45 minutes = 3/4 hour. Speed = 18 ÷ 3/4 = 18 × 4/3 = 24 km/h. (Or: 18 km in 45 min → 6 km per 15 min → 24 km per 60 min.)
questions.technique: Change minutes to hours BEFORE dividing.
questions.source: Speed_Distance_Time (recheck area, Mistake Map)

questions.stem: A bus leaves at 21:35 and the trip takes 3 h 50 min. What time does it arrive (12-hour time)?
questions.explanation: 21:35 + 3 h = 00:35. 00:35 + 50 min = 01:25, which is 1:25 am the next morning.
questions.technique: Add hours, then minutes; carry 60 minutes into an hour. After 24:00 it is the next day (am).
questions.trap: Writing pm, or not carrying the hour (12:25 am)
questions.source: Money_Measurement (time and 24-hour time, Drill 2 follow-up)

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = 180 − 140 = 40°. The exterior angles add to 360°, so the number of sides = 360 ÷ 40 = 9.
questions.technique: Interior + exterior = 180°. Number of sides = 360 ÷ exterior angle.
questions.source: Angles_Geometry (polygons), mixed revision

questions.stem: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. One number is removed and the mean of the 4 numbers left is 10. Which number was removed?
questions.explanation: Total of 5 numbers = 5 × 12 = 60. Total of 4 numbers = 4 × 10 = 40. Removed = 60 − 40 = 20.
questions.technique: Means → change to TOTALS first (mean × how many), then compare the totals.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P1 Q13 (average → total); Statistics topic

questions.stem: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green balls. Two balls are taken out one after the other WITHOUT putting the first one back. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.explanation: First red: 3/10. Now 9 balls are left and 2 are red: 2/9. Both red = 3/10 × 2/9 = 6/90 = 1/15.
questions.technique: Without replacement → the second fraction has one fewer on top AND bottom. Multiply along the branches.
questions.trap: 3/10 × 3/10 = 9/100 (as if the ball was put back)
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-05-15 Q6b/c (tree-diagram probability)

questions.stem: Factorise: (x + 2)² − 49
questions.explanation: 49 = 7². Difference of two squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) with a = x + 2 and b = 7. (x + 2 − 7)(x + 2 + 7) = (x − 5)(x + 9).
questions.technique: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). Find b by square-rooting the number.
questions.trap: Forgetting to square-root 49, or mixing up the signs
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-topictest4-datetbd Q3e ((x−3)² − 121 abandoned)

questions.stem: A school concert sold 40 tickets: adult tickets cost $15 and child tickets cost $8. The total takings were $446.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many CHILD tickets were sold?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How much MORE money came from adult tickets than from child tickets?

solution: Suppose all 40 were child tickets: 40 × $8 = $320. That is $446 − $320 = $126 short.
Each adult ticket adds $15 − $8 = $7 more, so adult tickets = 126 ÷ 7 = 18.
questions.technique: Assumption method: pretend they are all one kind, then swap one at a time.
questions.trap: (a) giving the adult tickets (18); (b) giving a total instead of the difference
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-07-10 P2 Q13 (assumption/contest problem skipped); wrong-quantity habit

questions.stem: A swimming club has 80 members, and 25% are under 10. Then 16 members who are 10 or OLDER leave the club. What percentage of the club is under 10 now?
questions.explanation: Under 10: 25% of 80 = 20 (this does not change). Members now: 80 − 16 = 64. 20 ÷ 64 × 100% = 31.25%.
questions.technique: Leaving changes the total. Part that stays the same ÷ NEW total.
questions.source: Test_Analysis_2026-10-02 P1 Q14 (changing whole, reversed)
